If the FDA delivers a written notice requesting records on a shampoo it believes is contaminated and dangerous, the responsible person and facility must permit an FDA officer or employee, upon presentation of appropriate credentials and a written notice, to have access to and copy all records relating to that cosmetic product and any other cosmetic product the Secretary reasonably believes is likely to be affected in a similar manner, provided such records are needed to assist the Secretary in determining whether the cosmetic product is adulterated and presents a threat of serious adverse health consequences or death to humans. Access must occur at reasonable times and within reasonable limits and in a reasonable manner. The request must be made by an officer or employee duly designated by the Secretary.

The provision requires access to and copying of all records relating to the cosmetic product and any other cosmetic product the Secretary reasonably believes is likely to be affected in a similar manner [1].  
Access is permitted only if the records are needed to assist the Secretary in determining whether the cosmetic product is adulterated and presents a threat of serious adverse health consequences or death to humans [1].  
The request must be made by an officer or employee duly designated by the Secretary, upon presentation of appropriate credentials and a written notice [1].  
Access occurs at reasonable times and within reasonable limits and in a reasonable manner [1].  
Records that are excluded include recipes or formulas for cosmetics, financial data, pricing data, personnel data (other than data as to qualification of technical and professional personnel performing functions subject to this chapter), research data (other than safety substantiation data for cosmetic products and their ingredients), and sales data (other than shipment data regarding sales) [1].  
The requirement does not extend to records related to a facility that solely performs labeling, relabeling, packaging, repackaging, holding, or distributing of cosmetic products if such activities are not part of the manufacturing or processing of a product for retail sale [1].
